title: Basil Beaver's Leaky River Workshop | Engineering Story for Kids

music.emotional_arrangement: marimba and plucked strings for discovery; hollow wood percussion for tests; gentle low strings for failed attempts; bright whistle, hand percussion and flowing-water rhythm for the successful finale

voices.delivery: melodic engineering story-song with acted reactions; no flat narration

continuity.basil: chestnut beaver child with broad flat tail, cream muzzle and belly, teal canvas apron, rolled mustard sleeves and small brown tool belt
continuity.pippa: small golden-yellow duck child in a coral neckerchief
continuity.moss: tiny moss-green frog with an indigo cap
continuity.workshop: miniature timber riverside workshop with a blue wooden waterwheel and a narrow stone-lined mill channel beside the untouched main stream
continuity.environment_rule: The repair affects only the constructed mill channel. The natural main stream and fish passage remain visibly open throughout.

scenes.action: Basil discovers water escaping from a cracked mill-channel wall while the blue waterwheel stands still; Pippa points and Moss watches from a dry stone.
lyrics: River light wakes the workshop door.
Silver water leaps through the wall.
Basil gasps, our wheel is still!
scenes.hero: one clear sparkling leak and the stopped wheel

scenes.action: At an outdoor workbench Basil lays out exactly four test materials: one broad leaf, three rounded stones, five forked sticks and one bowl of clay.
lyrics: Leaf, stone, stick, clay wait near.
Which will float? What will stay?
Let's test gently, one by one.

scenes.action: The broad leaf is placed over the crack, floats for a moment, then washes safely into Basil's catch basket.
lyrics: Green leaf lands on sparkling water.
Up it lifts, then sails away.
Pippa catches our floating clue.

scenes.action: Three stones sink and stay planted, but narrow blue streams remain visible through the gaps.
lyrics: Three round stones sink and stay.
They stay strong, but look between.
Little streams still slip on through.

scenes.action: Five forked sticks become a sturdy frame across the constructed crack while water still trickles between them.
lyrics: Five forked sticks form one frame.
Tie them tight; test the flow.
Water threads the open spaces.
scenes.hero: stable wooden frame with remaining leak

scenes.action: Basil and Pippa weave reeds through the stick frame; the leak slows to a few droplets but does not stop.
lyrics: Reeds go over, reeds go under.
Pull snug and watch the drops.
Slower now, but not quite sealed.

scenes.action: Basil presses clay around the outside edges while Pippa supports the reed panel and Moss checks the open main stream.
lyrics: Soft brown clay hugs every edge.
Press gently and hold it still.
One last drop, then quiet stone.

scenes.action: Basil lifts the small wooden mill gate; water follows the repaired clear channel, the wheel turns, and the main stream remains open beside it.
lyrics: Lift the gate; the channel gleams.
Round goes Basil's blue waterwheel.
Fish swim freely in the stream.
scenes.hero: controlled water flow turning the blue wheel

scenes.action: At golden hour the three friends make a gentle workshop rhythm while the turning wheel splashes in time; the repaired panel remains visible and stable.
lyrics: Wood dances with reed and drum.
Test, improve, and try once more.
Working together makes it flow.

quality_requirements: Basil, Pippa, Moss, the blue wheel and the constructed mill channel retain exact identity and layout continuity.
Every material behaves truthfully: leaf floats, stones sink with gaps, sticks frame, reeds slow, clay seals.
The untouched main stream and fish passage remain visibly open; the story never recommends blocking a natural river.
Exactly one focal test action occurs per scene and the visible result matches the sung phrase.
Real water, leaf, stone, wood, reed, clay, gate and wheel effects replace spoken imitation words.
The turning wheel and musical celebration appear only after the successful repair.
All shared gates in premium-musical-video-set-2026-08-31.json pass before release.
